title: Agrokor crisis, 'Lex Agrokor' and the 'Borg' e-mails
description: In spring 2017, as Agrokor, Croatia's largest private company, ran out of liquidity, the government drafted a law on extraordinary administration of companies of systemic importance ('Lex Agrokor'), adopted by parliament on 6 April 2017 (NN 32/2017). Plenković later said the law was 'drawn up in a matter of weeks and adopted at literally the last minute' with experts from outside the state administration, to prevent 'a string of bankruptcies'. The crisis broke his first coalition after six months: Plenković dismissed four ministers (the interior, justice, environment and public administration ministers left office on 27–28 April 2017) and in June 2017 formed a new majority with HNS (government cabinet record; Dnevnik Nova TV). In May 2018 newly published e-mails showed that Deputy Prime Minister and Economy Minister Martina Dalić had worked on the law with an informal group of consultants and lawyers, some of whom were later hired in the restructuring; she resigned on 14 May 2018. Plenković accepted the resignation, praised her role and said he was 'sorry there was not a little more time... a little more transparency'. In December 2018 the Commission for the Resolution of Conflicts of Interest found that Dalić and Finance Minister Zdravko Marić had violated the principles of holding public office, a finding without sanction; Plenković said no cabinet member had violated those principles. A separate Commission case concerning Plenković himself is listed under justice.
key_facts: 6 April 2017: Lex Agrokor adopted (NN 32/2017)
April 2017: coalition with Most collapses; four ministers dismissed; new majority with HNS from June 2017
14 May 2018: Martina Dalić resigns after publication of her e-mails with the consultants
December 2018: Commission finds Dalić and Marić violated principles of office (no sanction)

title: Former regional development minister Gabrijela Žalac convicted in EPPO cases
description: Gabrijela Žalac (HDZ) was minister of regional development and EU funds in Plenković's first government until July 2019. In November 2021 she was detained in an investigation by the European Public Prosecutor's Office (EPPO) into suspected EU-funds fraud, and Plenković confirmed she was one of the suspects (Euronews). On 2 September 2025 the Zagreb County Court sentenced her, under a plea agreement, to seven months in prison for abuse of office over private hospitality costs paid with public money between May 2017 and July 2019 (HRT, citing EPPO). In a second EPPO case, concerning a 2017 procurement of an IT system awarded at a price of EUR 1.73 million, the same court sentenced her to two years in prison, again under a plea agreement, after she paid EUR 200,000 in partial damages (N1, citing EPPO). Plenković is not a party to these proceedings.
key_facts: Žalac was minister in the 14th government until 19 July 2019
November 2021: detained in an EPPO investigation
2 September 2025: seven-month sentence (plea agreement)
Two-year sentence in the IT-procurement case (plea agreement); EUR 200,000 paid in partial damages

title: Appointment of Ivan Turudić as State Attorney General
description: In early 2024 Plenković's government proposed judge Ivan Turudić as State Attorney General. Before the parliamentary vote, Jutarnji list published messages exchanged between 2016 and 2020 by Turudić and former prominent HDZ politician Josipa Pleslić (formerly Rimac), who faces corruption charges, and reports emerged of meetings between Turudić and fugitive Zdravko Mamić; the opposition accused him of lying to the parliamentary judiciary committee (HRT). Plenković said the HDZ leadership was 'united in our continued support', that Turudić 'might have been restrictive in his expression' rather than lying, and that the leaks were politically motivated (N1, citing HRT); he rejected President Zoran Milanović's request to convene the National Security Council. Parliament's majority elected Turudić, and on 17 February 2024 eleven opposition parties held a protest in Zagreb, which Plenković called 'a rally of the radical left'. As Chief State Attorney, Turudić later decided that USKOK rather than the EPPO was competent in the investigation into Health Minister Vili Beroš (see that record).
key_facts: Published messages between Turudić and Josipa Pleslić (ex-Rimac), 2016–2020
Plenković and the HDZ maintained the nomination; parliament's majority elected Turudić
17 February 2024: opposition protest in Zagreb against the appointment
Parliamentary elections followed on 17 April 2024

title: 'Lex AP': criminal offence of disclosing content of investigations
description: In early 2023, after media reported that the initials 'AP' appeared in correspondence in the EPPO investigation concerning former minister Gabrijela Žalac and part of the public suspected they referred to the Prime Minister, Plenković said: 'We will change the Criminal Procedure Act and the Criminal Code, and situations like these, where things uncontrollably, intentionally, politically, selectively... leak out of the case and cause political problems, will no longer happen because it will be a criminal offense' (Croatian Journalists' Association via SafeJournalists). The amendments adopted on 14 March 2024 (NN 36/2024) added Article 307.a, punishing judicial and police officials, defendants, lawyers, witnesses, experts and interpreters who disclose the content of non-public investigative or evidentiary actions with up to three years in prison; people doing journalistic work are excluded, as are disclosures in a predominantly public interest. Journalists protested in Zagreb and Split on 31 January 2024; critics named the measure 'Lex AP'. ARTICLE 19 called it a disproportionate interference with freedom of expression and urged its repeal (June 2024). The same act introduced the separate offence of aggravated murder of a woman (femicide).
key_facts: Plenković's 2023 statement announcing a new criminal offence for leaks
14 March 2024: Article 307.a adopted (NN 36/2024), up to three years in prison
31 January 2024: journalists' protest in Zagreb and Split
June 2024: ARTICLE 19 calls for repeal

title: Health Minister Vili Beroš arrested and indicted in the 'Mikroskopi' case
description: Vili Beroš (HDZ) was health minister in Plenković's governments from 31 January 2020. In November 2024 USKOK announced his arrest; the EPPO said it had opened its own investigation against him and seven others, suspecting bribery. Chief State Attorney Ivan Turudić decided that USKOK was competent for the whole case and the EPPO handed over the file; European Chief Prosecutor Laura Kövesi reported Turudić to the European Commission (Dnevnik Nova TV). Beroš left the government and Irena Hrstić is health minister as of October 2026. On 22 September 2026 the Zagreb County Court confirmed USKOK's indictment charging Beroš with trading in influence within a criminal association, abuse of office and taking a EUR 75,000 bribe in the procurement of medical equipment, with alleged damage to the budget of EUR 740,000; two co-defendants were indicted with him, while other defendants in the case were convicted under plea agreements with USKOK. Plenković is not a party to the proceedings; Beroš is presumed innocent.
key_facts: November 2024: Beroš arrested by USKOK; EPPO opens a parallel investigation
Turudić assigns the case to USKOK; EPPO chief reports him to the European Commission
22 September 2026: indictment confirmed by the Zagreb County Court; trial to follow
Other defendants convicted under plea agreements; Beroš presumed innocent

title: Stance on Thompson's Hippodrome concert and the 'Za dom spremni' salute
description: On the eve of Marko Perković Thompson's concert at the Zagreb Hippodrome on 5 July 2025, attended by around half a million people, Plenković visited the dress rehearsal with his children and ministers Davor Božinović and Tomo Medved and was photographed with the singer (Vreme, citing Croatian media); opposition MP Dalija Orešković warned of the 'normalisation' of Ustaša symbols. After the concert, at which the song 'Bojna Čavoglave', which begins with the salute 'Za dom spremni', was performed, Plenković rejected accusations of promoting the Ustaša movement or historical revisionism, saying the salute is part of the singer's repertoire and that 'if something is part of a song, no one will censor or ban the song', while police would deal with individual cases of illegal symbols (N1 Serbia). In October 2025, responding to Zagreb mayor Tomislav Tomašević, he said: 'Be a man, Tomislav, and ban everything' (Index.hr). In October 2026, after Nazi and Ustaša chants by part of Hajduk Split's supporters before a match against Ajax, he said the competent authorities were acting; critics such as former MP Marko Vučetić accused him of tolerating a shift to the right.
key_facts: 4 July 2025: Plenković attends the rehearsal with his children and two ministers
July 2025: says the salute is part of the song and will not be banned
27 October 2025: 'Budi frajer, Tomislave, pa zabrani sve'
October 2026: Hajduk–Ajax incident; government says authorities are acting

title: Hazardous waste in Gospić and the October 2026 no-confidence vote
description: In 2026 the illegal deposit of an estimated 44,000 tonnes of hazardous and non-hazardous waste, about 33,000 tonnes of it buried, at the former PPK Velebit site in Gospić became a national political issue; in September 2026 Environment Minister Marija Vučković presented a four-phase remediation plan, including a EUR 40 million phase for the buried waste, and Minister of Physical Planning, Construction and State Assets Branko Bačić said he was convinced those responsible would face criminal charges (Dnevnik Nova TV). The SDP filed a motion of no confidence in the Prime Minister, citing the case among other reasons (SDP leader Siniša Hajdaš Dončić said the reasons went much deeper than the Gospić case); Možemo's Sandra Benčić said institutions had known of problems since 2022 and of organised crime since 2023, while HDZ MPs said there was no pollution of air, water or soil. On 21 October 2026 the motion failed: 55 MPs voted for, 79 against and 2 abstained, with 76 votes needed; Telegram counted it as the 44th opposition attempt to bring down his governments. Parliament rejected a Možemo proposal to require the government to report when the Prime Minister learned of the waste and why the chief state inspector had been replaced.
key_facts: About 44,000 tonnes of waste at the former PPK Velebit site in Gospić
September 2026: remediation plan in four phases
21 October 2026: no-confidence motion fails, 55 for, 79 against, 2 abstentions
Opposition questions over the replacement of the chief state inspector

title: Value of his Zagreb flat in the asset declaration
description: In January 2026 Plenković mocked Možemo's Sandra Benčić for buying a 115 m² flat in Zagreb for EUR 304,000, suggesting she was an example of falling property prices. Media then noted that his own asset declaration valued his 191 m² Zagreb flat at about EUR 346,000, roughly EUR 800 less per square metre than Benčić's; according to 24sata, cited by Dnevnik Nova TV, he had not updated the value for ten years, although officials must update property values on each new taking of office. In the declaration published in February 2026 the flat was revalued at EUR 600,000 (Dnevnik Nova TV).
key_facts: Declared value of the 191 m² flat: EUR 346,406.53 until 2025
February 2026 declaration: revalued at EUR 600,000
